extracted.intended_audience: Harvard faculty, postdocs, research staff, and administrators preparing external grant proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and institutional requirements for preparing external research grant proposals at Harvard, including Specific Aims, budgets, compliance, and foundation strategy. Emphasizes Harvard-specific conventions and pre-submission checks performed by the Office of Sponsored Programs (OSP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget development accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget development assistance (OSP provides help building accurate budgets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure effort, direct costs, and cost categories are justified and consistent with sponsor rules and Harvard conventions; check for common errors such as incorrect effort percentages, misapplied indirects, and mismatched line items. Use OSP budget tools and sample budgets. Expect OSP to catch 'Budget errors (effort, indirect cost calculation)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance review completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance review (human subjects, animals, biosafety).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All required compliance protocols (IRB, IACUC, biosafety) must be in place or documented. Include protocol numbers and evidence of approvals where required. OSP will flag 'Compliance gaps (IRB protocol numbers, IACUC)'. Ensure authentication of resources and explicit rigor and reproducibility language in methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subaward and consortium agreement planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and plan for subaward and consortium agreements early in proposal development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify scope, budgets, effort, indirects, and timelines for subrecipients; resolve subaward complications pre-submission. OSP checks for 'Subaward complications' and will advise on required documentation and institutional signatures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-sharing and cost-share justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost-sharing analysis and justification when institutional cost share is proposed or required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document sources of cost share, confirm institutional approval, and ensure consistency with sponsor rules and Harvard policy. Use OSP to analyze feasibility and institutional commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect cost rate compliance and negotiation
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply appropriate Harvard indirect (F&A) rates and negotiate when necessary (Harvard indirect rate ~70% on-campus federal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budgeters must use the correct Harvard indirect rates for on-campus vs off-campus activities and account for exceptions; coordinate with OSP for rate negotiation and justification. Align proposed budget to Harvard indirects to avoid OSP objections to unrealistic or noncompliant budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims page structure and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific Aims Page: standard four-paragraph structure; hypothesis-driven aims; aim independence; conceptual figure where helpful; iterate 10+ times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a four-paragraph layout that states the central hypothesis, lists clear, hypothesis-driven aims, and ensures aims are independent (avoid cascading failures). Include a concise conceptual figure if it helps clarity. Iterate heavily—OSP recommends 10+ revisions—and use OSP-specific Aims consultations and templates. Aim to communicate the 'Significance landed in 30 seconds.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance framing for non-specialists
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame significance and innovation for non-specialist reviewers and pass the 'So what?' test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the problem matters beyond specialists; show impact and broader implications quickly. Cite competitor work fairly and situate your contribution in the field. Avoid hype; be concise so reviewers can grasp significance within seconds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation presented as feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovation described not only as novel but as a feasible application or approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define innovation as a novel application or idea grounded in preliminary data or a plausible plan. Avoid framing innovation as speculative; show how it is implementable within the project scope. This ties to 'Innovation framed as feasible' in OSP's implicit rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach: detailed methods and rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach should include per-aim subsections, statistical analysis plan, power calculation with citation, sample size justification, rigor and reproducibility language, authentication of resources, and alternatives if primary approach fails.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each aim provide explicit methods, analytic strategies, and contingency plans. Include power calculations with citations and clearly justify sample sizes. Address experimental rigor, reproducibility, blinding/randomization where relevant, authentication of reagents/resources, and plausible alternative strategies if initial experiments fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator qualifications and environment fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate investigator expertise and environment: cite Harvard institutional commitment, specific cores and resources, and include specific collaborator letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show that the PI and team have the skills and track record appropriate to the project's scope; align described productivity with the proposed effort. Include letters of support from collaborators and institutional commitment statements referencing named cores and facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cores, centers, and resource citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite Harvard-specific cores and centers (e.g., HMS Molecular Imaging Core, Harvard Catalyst, HSCI, Wyss Institute, department-specific cores) to demonstrate access to resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly name and describe the core facilities and services that will be used, including any cost or access arrangements. Use cores to strengthen the 'Environment' section and to justify feasibility and institutional support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliated hospitals and cross-institution collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage affiliated hospitals (MGH, BWH, BIDMC, BCH, DFCI) and cross-institutional collaborations as evidence of environment and access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include letters of support from affiliated hospital PIs when relevant; describe collaborative arrangements and how clinical or translational resources will be accessed. Cross-institutional collaborations are standard and should be documented clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and mentorship documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Harvard training programs (HMS HST, MSTP, PSTP, HSPH PhD, HSCI training) to strengthen training/mentorship sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposing training plans or career development, reference affiliated training programs and describe mentorship structure, trainee roles, and institutional supports. These programs add depth and credibility to training components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundation grant strategy alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: For foundation proposals: read the foundation annual report, match the foundation's recent funded portfolio, engage the program officer early, and coordinate through Foundation Relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure institutional alignment with the foundation's priorities; do not approach foundations without coordination. Use Foundation Relations to arrange program officer meetings and secure institutional letters; include letters of support from senior leaders when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of OSP-provided templates and sample applications
rubrics_metrics.description: OSP offers sample funded applications (anonymized library), Specific Aims templates, budget development tools, and compliance protocol templates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use OSP sample materials and templates to model structure, level of detail, and formatting. Review funded examples to understand expectations for aims, preliminary data, and methods. Leverage OSP tools for budgeting and compliance documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty effort and cost conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical faculty effort on grants is 10–30%; postdoc and student support is standard; equipment purchases over $5K require special justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align effort percent to proposed responsibilities and documented productivity. Justify equipment purchases >$5K explicitly and follow institutional procurement and justification rules. Ensure proposed personnel and costs are consistent with Harvard norms and sponsor policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-funder diversification
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategy of diversifying funders: Federal (NIH, NSF) primary, foundation secondary, industry partnerships growing, philanthropic gifts via Foundation Relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop proposals across multiple funder types to balance portfolio risk and match project fit to funder priorities. Tailor messaging and scope for each funder type and coordinate institutionally for foundations and philanthropy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with Foundation Relations for foundation approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty should not approach foundations directly without coordination; program officer meetings often arranged through OSP/Foundation Relations and major foundations want institutional alignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with Foundation Relations early to align institutional priorities with the foundation's mission, obtain senior leadership letters when useful, and to plan program officer engagement. Read foundation materials and match the funded portfolio before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit and proportionate productivity evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate productivity proportionate to the scope (e.g., publications, preliminary data) to justify the investigator's ability to complete the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide quantitative preliminary data where possible and a publication/productivity record that matches the proposed research scale. Use preliminary data to support feasibility and power claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic budget aligned with institutional indirects
rubrics_metrics.description: Realistic budget aligned with Harvard indirect costs and institutional conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget should reflect true project needs, include appropriate indirect costs, and be consistent with Harvard rates; unrealistic low budgets or omitted indirects will be flagged by OSP. Ensure budgets support stated aims and personnel effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address data sharing and vertebrate animal sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Include required sections such as data sharing plans and vertebrate animals descriptions when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check sponsor requirements and include all required sections. OSP flags 'Missing required sections (data sharing, vertebrate animals)'. Provide appropriate detail and approvals or plan to obtain them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid format violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Comply with sponsor format rules (page limits, font, margins).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow application formatting exactly; OSP will check for 'Format violations (page limits, font, margins)'. Submissions that exceed limits or violate format risk desk rejection or reviewer confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and document alternatives/pitfalls
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge limitations and provide alternatives (Pitfalls/Alternatives) to demonstrate rigor and realism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss potential challenges and explicit contingency plans for each aim. This reduces perceived risk and shows thoughtful experimental design; Harvard Academic Voice recommends acknowledging limitations rather than using hype.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of support and institutional endorsement
rubrics_metrics.description: Secure letters of support from senior collaborators and institutional leaders where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should be specific, describe the collaborator's role/resources committed, and match the scope of the project. Harvard often expects letters from affiliated hospital PIs or senior leaders for foundation proposals; OSP values concrete, not generic, support statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit rigor and reproducibility language
rubrics_metrics.description: Include explicit language describing rigor and reproducibility measures in methods and approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address blinding, randomization, replication, validation, authentication of reagents, data management, and statistical robustness. Use standard phrasing where applicable and cite practices or guidelines; OSP lists 'Rigor language explicit' as a winning feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-submission checklist for common OSP catches
rubrics_metrics.description: Common pre-submission issues OSP catches: budget errors, compliance gaps, subaward complications, format violations, missing required sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run proposals through an institutional checklist: verify budgets and indirects, confirm compliance approvals and protocol numbers, resolve subaward paperwork, obey formatting rules, and ensure all sponsor-required sections (data sharing, vertebrate animals, etc.) are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harvard academic voice and tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a confident but not arrogant tone, cite competitor work generously, position your contribution within the field, avoid hype language, and acknowledge limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write clearly and assertively while avoiding overstatement. Give appropriate credit to prior work, situate your project strategically, and be explicit about what will and will not be accomplished. Use Pitfalls/Alternatives to temper claims and show thoughtfulness.
